segments: 416 Chronography. [The Greeks] were about thirty thousand,
and because of the greatness of the city, they could not be seen in it.
They set fire to the city twice,
and about a quarter of it burned.
And they also opened the gates,
and the Franks who were outside entered,
and drew their swords,
and killed a great number of the Greeks.
And when many of them took refuge in the great church of Hagia Sophia,
the Franks went against them.
And the Patriarch, the chief priests, and the priests went out to meet them, carrying crosses and Gospels,
and threw themselves down before them, crying out and entreating for the rest of the people who were there.
The Franks, however, were merciless,
and killed the priests along with the people,
and plundered the church.
Now the Franks had three leaders:
one, the Doge of the Venetians,
by whose ships and vessels all the forces of the Franks had come,
and he was an old blind man;
and another, the leader of the French (or Franks?),
whose name was the Marquis;
and another whose name was Godefroi [Baldwin?].
And they cast lots as to whose should be the kingdom of Constantinople.
And it fell to Godefroi [Baldwin],
and he was made king over it.
And the Venetians took possession of the islands of Crete and Rhodes and the rest of the islands.
And to the Marquis they gave the territory to the east of the strait of the sea that crosses into Pontus,
namely, Laodicea and Nicaea, together with Philadelphia and the rest.
The Greeks, however, resisted and did not surrender them to the Franks,
but they made a Greek patrician whose name was Laskaris king over them.
And at this time,
while Nur al-Din Arslan Shah, the lord of Mosul, and his cousin Qutb al-Din Muhammad son of Zangi, the lord of Sinjar, were on friendly terms with one another,
Malik Adil sowed discord between them.
And on this account Nur al-Din went and encamped against Nisibis, which belonged to his cousin,
and waged war against it,
and was close to taking it.
Then news came to him from Mosul
that Muzaffar al-Din Gokburi {OCR?: Kukburi}, the son of Zayn al-Din Ali Kuchuk, the lord of Erbil, had entered Nineveh,
and plundered it,
and burned its crops.
